headline: 10 arrested as house takeover attempt foiled in Adabor
summary: Police opened fire in self-defence after suspects armed with machetes attacked them during an operation to arrest those involved in a land dispute.
details: Police arrested 10 people in connection with an attempt to seize a building in Adabor, Dhaka, following a violent clash during a raid.
During an operation on Tuesday at 2am, suspects armed with machetes attacked police officers near a canal bank near the Nabodoy Housing kitchen market.
Law enforcers stated they opened fire in self-defence, resulting in two suspects—Rajib Howlader and Sagar alias Chhoto Bigar—sustaining gunshot wounds to their legs.
Four people were arrested at the scene, including the two injured suspects, while steel machetes, blades, and other sharp weapons were recovered.
The incident follows a Saturday morning attack where 20 to 25 people vandalised the gate, windows, and CCTV cameras of a house on Road No. 6 of the Shyamoli Housing project.
Relatives of the building owner alleged that a local man named Khorshed Alam had previously taken control of the building after August 5, 2024, but owners regained possession on March 12.
The attack was captured on CCTV footage, showing masked men and a group of young men with weapons vandalising the property.
Following a written complaint filed by the victim, the Dhaka Metropolitan Police confirmed that 10 people have been arrested so far.
caption:
Police opened fire in self-defence after being attacked with machetes during a raid to stop a house takeover in Adabor.

Police arrested 10 people in connection with an attempt to seize a building in Adabor, Dhaka, following a violent clash during a raid.

During an operation on Tuesday at 2am, suspects armed with machetes attacked police officers near a canal bank near the Nabodoy Housing kitchen market.

Law enforcers stated they opened fire in self-defence, resulting in two suspects—Rajib Howlader and Sagar alias Chhoto Bigar—sustaining gunshot wounds to their legs.

Four people were arrested at the scene, including the two injured suspects, while steel machetes, blades, and other sharp weapons were recovered.

The incident follows a Saturday morning attack where 20 to 25 people vandalised the gate, windows, and CCTV cameras of a house on Road No. 6 of the Shyamoli Housing project.

Relatives of the building owner alleged that a local man named Khorshed Alam had previously taken control of the building after August 5, 2024, but owners regained possession on March 12.

The attack was captured on CCTV footage, showing masked men and a group of young men with weapons vandalising the property.

Following a written complaint filed by the victim, the Dhaka Metropolitan Police confirmed that 10 people have been arrested so far.

headline: UPL staff harassed over sale of 'The Unfinished Memoirs' in Dhaka
summary: Two publishing house employees were allegedly harassed and handed to police by BNP activists after claiming the book was banned.
details: Two sales staff from University Press Limited (UPL) were reportedly harassed and handed over to police on Monday evening at their Banglabazar showroom in Dhaka.
According to UPL, two men entered the outlet and claimed that Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's 'The Unfinished Memoirs' was banned, demanding that its sale be stopped.
The men allegedly pulled down the shop shutter, gathered a crowd, and took the employees to the Faridabad Police Outpost, where they were later released.
Sutrapur Police Station chief Matiur Rahman identified the individuals involved as local BNP activists, noting that the employees were released after police spoke to both sides.
UPL described the incident as 'extremely shameful and unfortunate for the nation,' stating that the book has not been banned by any responsible authority.
The publisher emphasized that it follows legal procedures for banning books and has historically faced pressure from various governments and individuals to remove certain titles.
UPL asserted that 'The Unfinished Memoirs' is a crucial historical text providing context on the creation of Bangladesh and the Liberation War.
The publishing house called on the state and society to prevent a 'rule of thuggery' in the publishing industry and protect the freedom of knowledge.
caption:
Two publishing house employees were harassed and handed to police for selling a book they claimed was banned. Who was behind it?

Two sales staff from University Press Limited (UPL) were reportedly harassed and handed over to police on Monday evening at their Banglabazar showroom in Dhaka.

According to UPL, two men entered the outlet and claimed that Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's 'The Unfinished Memoirs' was banned, demanding that its sale be stopped.

The men allegedly pulled down the shop shutter, gathered a crowd, and took the employees to the Faridabad Police Outpost, where they were later released.

Sutrapur Police Station chief Matiur Rahman identified the individuals involved as local BNP activists, noting that the employees were released after police spoke to both sides.

UPL described the incident as 'extremely shameful and unfortunate for the nation,' stating that the book has not been banned by any responsible authority.

The publisher emphasized that it follows legal procedures for banning books and has historically faced pressure from various governments and individuals to remove certain titles.

UPL asserted that 'The Unfinished Memoirs' is a crucial historical text providing context on the creation of Bangladesh and the Liberation War.

The publishing house called on the state and society to prevent a 'rule of thuggery' in the publishing industry and protect the freedom of knowledge.
